headline: power and gas rally hard — spot back to £125/MWh and the winter gas curve up ~16% since early August
commentary: The window that opened in early August has slammed shut. UK power spot has rallied from £110/MWh on 6 August back to £125.12/MWh, up roughly 15% in under two weeks and near the top of its 12-month range. Gas has driven it: front-month NBP is 154.3 p/therm, up about 16% from 133 a fortnight ago and back within a whisker of the late-July high. The move that matters is the winter curve — Dec 26 has jumped to 160 p/therm from 138, Jan 27 to around 158 from 137, and Winter 26 to 156 from 133. That is roughly a 16-17% re-inflation of the winter risk premium in ten trading days, wiping out the compression we flagged on 6 August. Anyone who fixed into that dip did well. For contracts still open this is a materially worse entry than a fortnight ago and near-term momentum is upward, so there is little case for holding out for a lower low: where the term suits, fixing the energy block removes the risk of chasing a rising curve into winter.

gas.note: NBP front-month (Sep 26) is 154.3 p/therm, up 1.2% on the day and up about 16% from 133 a fortnight ago, back near the late-July high. The winter curve has re-inflated with it — Dec 26 at 160, Jan 27 near 158.
